The main takeaway from our work is that

cadmium (CD) does not appear to stimulate uterine cell proliferation through classical estrogen receptor pathways; instead, we have found evidence that it stimulates uterine cell growth through nongenomic pathways involving epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways.
Cd is not acting through the classical ER pathways in these estrogen-responsive uterines cells.
cadmium (a metal) can mimic some of the actions of estrogen (a steroid hormone) by activating the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), which is a receptor for growth factors.
